original_text:
–Unaided eye can distinguish two points that are 0.2mm (200µm) apart.–Any closer together and points will appear as a single object–Ex: printed image
–Image is made up of dots too small for unaided eye to see, they appear as one smooth, continuous image until it is magnified–Resolution of light microscopy is limited by wavelength, which is why tools like EM are needed. Smallest resolution is .2µm
explanation: This slide explains human eye resolution limits compared to light microscopy. The unaided human eye can distinguish two points that are at least 0.2 millimeters (200 micrometers) apart. If they are closer, they appear as a single object (e.g., printed halftone dots on a page appear as a smooth continuous image until magnified). The resolution of light microscopy (LM) is physically limited by the wavelength of visible light. The smallest resolution achievable by LM is 0.2 micrometers (0.2 µm). To resolve smaller structures, electron microscopes (EM) must be used.

questions.q: What is the resolution limit of the unaided human eye?
questions.exp: The text states: 'Unaided eye can distinguish two points that are 0.2mm (200µm) apart. Any closer together and points will appear as a single object.'

questions.q: Why is the resolution of light microscopy limited, and what is its smallest resolution limit?
opts: It is limited by lens shape; its limit is 0.2 mm.
It is limited by the wavelength of light; its limit is 0.2 µm.
It is limited by the dyes used; its limit is 10 µm.
It is limited by the eye's focal length; its limit is 1.0 µm.
